answer: A per-identity stake deposit makes each fake agent cost real money. An agent must lock a bond larger than any gain from one fake account before it can submit work; honest agents get it back with interest, so their net cost is near zero. An attacker creating a ridge of ghost identities must fund every one, and slashing any colluding cluster burns its bond, so cost scales linearly with no economy of scale. An audit echo in the reputation log exposes duplicate clusters, while an honest comet of audited settlements stays profitable.
